sentences.text: This is a petition seeking quashing of FIR No. 59/2018 dated 16.03.2018, under Sections 406/420/120-B IPC, registered at Police Station - Economic Offences Wing and consequential proceedings, if any, emanating therefrom.
2. As per the FIR, the petitioners had taken a loan from IFCI Bank for development of a Mall at Community Centre, Paschim Puri, Delhi-110063.

It is stated that on account of financial stress, the petitioners could not make the loan payment and also sold some portion of the mortgaged property without the NOC from the mortgage i.e. the complainant.
Hence, the FIR was registered.

sentences.text: All the petitioners except Nos. 6, 7 and 9 are present in Court.
The affidavits of petitioner Nos. 6, 7 and 9 are on record.
Remaining petitioners are present either in person or through Video Conferencing.
The petitioners who are present in Court have been identified by their counsel, Mr Sunil Agarwal.
5. Mr Rohit Bharadwaj, learned counsel appears for respondent No.2- IFCI Limited and states that the bank has settled the matter with the petitioners and has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
6. Both the parties state that they have entered into the aforesaid settlement out of their own free will, volition and without any threat, force, undue influence or coercion.
The petitioners regret their action and undertake to never repeat the same in future.

7. Since the parties have arrived at a settlement and no disputes are pending, I am convinced that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice as the complaint is of a private nature and the complainant does not wish to prosecute it any further.
This should not be treated as a legal precedent and in this case the proceedings are quashed as the respondent has decided to put a quietus to the matter.
The Court does not see any fruitful purpose if criminal proceedings are permitted to be prosecuted any further.
It is a fit case for quashing.
In this view of the matter, there is no reason to continue the proceedings.
This is a digitally signed order.

However, I am of the view that considerable time of the police and judicial time has been wasted as the FIR is of the year 2018.

The police machinery has been put in motion on account of the acts of commission & omission on behalf of the parties and useful time of the police which could have been utilised for important matters has been misdirected towards this case.
Hence, the petitioners must pay some costs.

9. For the reasons stated above, FIR No. 59/2018 dated 16.03.2018, under Sections 406/420/120-B IPC, registered at Police Station - Economic Offences Wing) and consequential proceedings, if any,
emanating therefrom are hereby quashed subject to the following conditions and its compliance:
a) Petitioners will deposit costs for planting of trees which must have the nursery life of 3 years and should be a 'tree' within the definition of The Delhi Preservation of Trees Act, 1994.
b) Petitioners shall report to the Deputy Conservator of Forest, South (hereinafter referred to as 'DCF') and the needful shall be done within a period of 4 weeks from today.
